subject: CarePath MAP: verification playbook, success signals & owners
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ben Liu <ben.liu@carepath.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CarePath MAP: verification playbook, success signals & owners

Ben — attaching the first draft of the mutual action playbook for the evaluation phase. High level ask: confirm these success signals and owners by EOD Friday so we can lock the test sprint and SOW items.

Summary (short):
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference integration for CarePath triage assistant in production-like conditions and close by Aug 6.
- Success signals (must-pass):
  1) Safety/concordance: Response redaction and PII scrub passes all 100 sample tests (no PHI leakage).
  2) Relevance: Intent-match >= 92% measured on the labeled holdout set (50 queries per intent).
  3) Latency: 90th percentile generation latency < 250ms for 256-token context under reserved load profile.
  4) Stability: No more than 1 incident (errors or timeouts) per 10k requests during pilot week.

Exit gates (all required to move to canary):
- Completion of the acceptance test matrix (attached) with sign-off from CarePath QA.
- Security checklist items A1–A5 validated by Jordan.
- Procurement: signed SOW (procurement@carepath.com) and agreed billing terms.

Acceptance tests (examples):
- Functional: 100 end-to-end flows with labeled expected outputs; pass threshold 95/100.
- Edge cases: 30 adversarial prompts; system must not return PHI or hallucinated claims.
- Load: 1-minute stress bursts to validate autoscale and latency SLO.

Attachments: carepath_map_v1.xlsx (tabbed: success_signals, test_matrix, timeline)
Related doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2bCarePath-MAP-v1 (concurrent edit enabled)

Next steps: please reply with any edits to the success signals and confirm owners for each test. Suggested owners in the sheet — we propose Karthik for performance, Jordan for security, Camila for data validation.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Liu <ben.liu@carepath.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@carepath.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CarePath MAP: verification playbook, success signals & owners

Thanks Naomi — this looks thorough and actionable. Quick inline notes and a couple requests: 

> Success signals (must-pass):
> 1) Safety/concordance: Response redaction and PII scrub passes all 100 sample tests (no PHI leakage).

We can confirm the PHI test set; will share a redacted sample set by Wednesday. Can you confirm the scope of "PII scrub" — does that include phone numbers, insurance IDs, and free-text notes?

> 3) Latency: 90th percentile generation latency < 250ms for 256-token context under reserved load profile.

This target is aggressive but acceptable if the reserved pool is as sized in the SOW draft. Procurement will want an SLA appendix if we rely on that number.

Requests from our side: 
- Procurement asked for a draft SOW to attach to vendor review (I see a SOW draft in your attachments — please push the PDF to us and cc procurement).
- Can we add a privacy-control verification: verify that logs stored for 30 days are masked and access-controlled (list which keys/users can access logs)?

Owners: Karthik/Jordan/Camila sound good. We'll assign CarePath QA (Sara Patel) to the test matrix on our side.

I'll review the sheet and return a marked copy Thursday. If you want, set up a 30-minute sync Thursday morning to walk the acceptance tests.

—Ben
Ben Liu
Head of Product
CarePath Health

Subject: Re: CarePath MAP: verification playbook, success signals & owners

Ben / team — thanks for the quick read. A few operational clarifications and owner assignments so we can run the sprint efficiently: 

1) Owners (internal):
   - Performance & load tests: Karthik Iyer (me) — I'll own the load harness and template JMeter scenarios.
   - Security / privacy checklist execution: Jordan Blake — will validate masking, KMS integration, and SOC2 artifacts.
   - Data validation & intent-label quality: Camila Reyes — will run the labeled holdout and concordance scoring.

2) SOW & SLA notes: Naomi, I've attached a SOW draft (SOW_CarePath_Draft_v1.pdf) with an SLA appendix placeholder for the 90th percentile latency target; procurement, please review the billing cadence section on p.4.

3) Privacy-control verification: proposed test — confirm that logs exported to GCS/Drive are masked at rest and only accessible to the named service account and Jordan's team. Jordan: can you please list the Access Control owners (IAM roles) you need me to provision?

4) Timeline proposal (short):
   - Week of Jun 21: dataset handoff and test harness setup (owner: Camila)
   - Jun 28–Jul 2: performance run + security checklist (owners: Karthik, Jordan)
   - Jul 5–9: edge-case acceptance and QA sign-off (owner: CarePath QA)
   - Jul 12: internal review; Jul 19: executive sign-off; Aug 6: target close/canary sign-off

If that timeline looks OK, Naomi / Ben — propose a standing 30-min sync Thurs 10:00 AM PT to clear blockers. I'll prepare the load scenario template by tomorrow EOD.

Thanks — Karthik

From: Ben Liu <ben.liu@carepath.com>

Karthik/Naomi — this is great; we confirm the timeline and owners. A couple of small notes from procurement: please send the SOW PDF to procurement@carepath.com (attached is our vendor intake form). We'll try to complete vendor review in two weeks.

Privacy: Sara (CarePath QA) will own the sample PHI set; we'll share it via the secure bucket you provide. Jordan, I'll give you a point contact for access control (IT Ops: rachel@carepath.com).

Standing sync: Thursday 10:00 AM PT works for our team — add calendar invite and include dial-in + recording if possible.

Confirming acceptance criteria: we accept the success signals with the clarification for PII scope (phone, insurance id and free-text notes included). Once we get the SOW and the masked log verification plan, we'll mark the MAP items as ready.

Thanks — Ben
